central_topic: Finite-budget sensitivity of fixed-ridge Bradley-Terry rankings to nested binary-outcome flips, using influence-screened exact-refit path search on Chatbot Arena preferences and season-specific NBA games.
core_methods: Centered Bradley-Terry logistic sum-loss fitting with fixed L2 ridge, fractional ties, and an optional home-advantage coefficient
Hessian-based directional influence calculations and linear predictions checked against finite-change exact refits
Adaptive checkpoint search using fitted rank gaps and exact-refitted rank displacement and inversions
Whole-path local refinement by selected-position swaps and unused-row replacements, with affected-prefix caching and complete-path fallback
Unique nested binary-outcome flips at floored fractions 0.001, 0.005, and 0.01 of all usable comparisons
Grouped paired bootstrap of fixed intervention plans for rank intervals and candidate-minus-baseline effects
comparators: Uniform random eligible outcome flips, an evaluated baseline
Degree-sum-quartile-stratified random flips, an evaluated approximate exposure-matching baseline rather than exact endpoint matching
Smallest absolute fitted matchup-margin selection, an evaluated baseline
Fixed-influence selection and adaptive exact-refit paths retained within the candidate search, not separately established final ablations
Preference-vote manipulation and finite-sample data-removal sensitivity as related literatures, not additional evaluated interventions
Exchange-based local search for rank aggregation as methodological context, not a tested Kemeny-ranking algorithm
benchmarks: Chatbot Arena human-preference comparisons: arena case, with 14272 usable search rows and 43205 usable final rows according to the public task contract
NBA unique-game season panels: 2006-2008 in search and 2011-2015 in final evidence; outcomes are refitted with Bradley-Terry rather than using Elo ratings
result_driven_themes: The strongest recorded search configuration uses whole-path exchange refinement; the records support configuration-level comparison, not isolated attribution to every search component
Final aggregate perturbation effects exceed the recorded random, degree-stratified, and margin baselines, but several NBA paired intervals cross zero, limiting universal superiority claims

Finite-change influence discrepancies are substantially larger in the final Arena case than in the final NBA cases, motivating the distinction between local derivatives and refitted finite perturbations
Arena preferences and sports outcomes provide descriptive cross-design context, not a causal comparison of evaluation designs or a matched human-versus-model-judge study
Fixed-plan grouped resampling quantifies conditional uncertainty without reoptimizing attacks inside bootstrap samples or making three algorithmic seeds independent datasets
